video.title: Thomas Laffont: The $4T AI IPO Wave Is Coming… and We've Never Seen Anything Like It
video.display_title_html: Thomas Laffont: The $4T AI IPO Wave Is Coming

thesis: Coatue's Thomas Laffont argues the unicorn economy is healthier than in 2021 because AI has concentrated funding into a handful of real, fast-compounding 'Magnificent Eight' private companies whose imminent IPOs (SpaceX, Anthropic, OpenAI) will finally rebalance the ecosystem's cash-in versus cash-out.

chapters.title: Coatue's Thomas Laffont joins the Besties!
Public markets are back as AI dominates the "Unicorn Economy"
The case for SpaceX: Compounding launch monopoly and Starlink
The 10x Paradox: Why we're seeing unprecedented scaling
Segmenting AI markets and future impact
Bestie Q&A: Power Law, future of VC, revenue, liquidity explosion

insights.headline: Funding per unicorn jumped 5x since 2021
insights.body: The number of new unicorns has normalized back to a much lower, pre-COVID level while AI's wallet share of fundraising keeps climbing — so mathematically each unicorn now raises about 5x what it did in the 2021 Zerp peak. Fewer companies, each far larger.

insights.headline: 2021 unicorn cohort is stuck; pre-Zerp cohort thrived
insights.body: Of the ~73 pre-Zerp unicorns, 80% had raised again or exited 20 quarters in. The 2021 cohort balloons to 479 companies but fewer than 20% had exited or raised at the same point — a far less healthy vintage.

insights.headline: The 'Magnificent Eight' private index, ~$4T value
insights.body: Laffont proposes a future index of SpaceX, Stripe, Anthropic, Databricks, Revolut, ByteDance, Anduril — spanning internet, AI, fintech and spacetech. It represents almost $4 trillion and has outperformed the public MAG7 nearly name-for-name.

insights.headline: Three IPOs to exceed 10 years of combined exits
insights.body: SpaceX (weeks away), Anthropic (confidential S1 filed that day), and OpenAI going public will, just those three, return more cash than the prior ten years of exits combined — finally rebalancing an ecosystem that consumed far more cash than it returned.

insights.headline: OpenAI + Anthropic revenue may pass all of Microsoft by 2028
insights.body: Starting from January 2025, the two labs blew past Workday, ServiceNow, Adobe, then Salesforce, and are now bigger than Google Cloud and Azure. Coatue's forecast: bigger than AWS and potentially all of Microsoft by 2028.

insights.headline: SpaceX value rises per-launch as it launches more
insights.body: Cadence of launches is the #1 driver correlated to SpaceX's valuation, but valuation-per-launch also climbs over time. Coatue's framework: the business model quality improves with scale — moving from one-time government launches to recurring Starlink constellations to a multi-constellation platform.

insights.headline: The 10x Paradox: bigger companies are likelier to 10x
insights.body: A unicorn has ~8% odds of becoming a decacorn; a decacorn has 8–13% odds of reaching $100B. But a centacorn ($100B+) has a 31% chance of a subsequent 10x — value compounds fastest at the very top, defying intuition.

insights.headline: Two companies went $500B→$1T in weeks
insights.body: It typically takes multiple years to climb from a $500B to a $1T market cap. Recently three public companies did it in one year — and two of them in a matter of weeks.

insights.headline: Cerebras' OpenAI contract quintupled its value
insights.body: Laffont led Cerebras' Series B and sat on the board through years of no new capital and hard grinding. A massive OpenAI contract then quintupled the company's value ahead of its IPO — a case study in long-gestation semis bets.

insights.headline: AI revenue rests on three pillars: consumer, ads, enterprise
insights.body: Coatue sizes the AI ecosystem at ~$140B today, ~$300B this year, doubling in 2027. Sources: consumer (subs × ARPU), ads (~25% of Meta/Google ads are AI-enabled today heading to 100%, ~$150B), and enterprise (Claude Code, Codex).

insights.headline: Starlink will eat the global telco profit pool
insights.body: Laffont expects Starlink to power a device enabling calls anywhere on Earth, treating the $200–400B global telco/broadband/wireless profit pool as Starlink's addressable market with a structurally better, tower-free product.

insights.headline: Memory has no TSMC — a structural scarcity
insights.body: An OpenAI-style ASIC can lean on TSMC to fabricate, but there's no equivalent foundry for memory. That scarcity reframes how memory multiples should compare to custom-chip multiples and explains recent moves in memory names.

insights.headline: A price war between OpenAI and Anthropic is possible
insights.body: Drawing on the ride-share and food-delivery wars, Laffont notes excess capital eventually funds price wars. With $200B war chests, one lab could pull a price lever — though heavy infrastructure spend makes it non-obvious.

insights.headline: Public markets are the great equalizer and antiseptic
insights.body: Laffont welcomes the scrutiny of short sellers and the market on SpaceX, OpenAI and Anthropic. Chamath adds a tactical wrinkle: with heavy passive buying, the real price-discovery 'disinfectant' won't hit on day one but roughly six months and one day post-IPO.

quotes.text: The winners are compounding faster than ever, which means the costs of not being in a winner are higher than ever.
quotes.speaker: Thomas Laffont

quotes.text: The public market is the great equalizer. It will not care about my bullshit presentation. It will be the great antiseptic.
quotes.speaker: Thomas Laffont

quotes.text: If I want to make memory, well, there is no TSMC.
quotes.speaker: Thomas Laffont

quotes.text: The power law rules our lives. All the great gains are being consolidated into small numbers of companies.
quotes.speaker: Jason Calacanis

quotes.text: These are not fake companies. These are companies generating substantial revenue at scale that are growing faster than anything we've ever seen.
quotes.speaker: Thomas Laffont

quotes.text: Anthropic pre-Claude Code was a completely different company than post-Claude Code. One event completely dented the trajectory of almost that entire industry.
quotes.speaker: Thomas Laffont

action_items: If you take one thing from this: the cost of not owning a winner now exceeds the risk of overpaying for one — concentration, not diversification, has been the rational power-law strategy.
Watch the SpaceX, Anthropic and OpenAI IPOs as the real test; don't trust day-one pricing — wait roughly six months for passive-buying supply to wash through before judging value.
When evaluating SpaceX, track launch cadence and the shift from one-time government launches to recurring Starlink constellation revenue — that's what re-rates the multiple.
Note structural scarcity: there's no foundry equivalent for memory, so memory multiples may deserve a premium over custom-ASIC multiples.
